> **In one line** — Broadcom is a chip-and-software giant whose AI-driven semiconductor sales just produced a record quarter (revenue up 86% YoY), but the stock at ~$355 trades at a price that already assumes years of very fast growth.

## What Broadcom is

Broadcom (AVGO) designs semiconductors and infrastructure software. Its FY2025 revenue (fiscal year ended 2 Nov 2025) split into two segments, per the 10-K filed 18 Dec 2025:

- **Semiconductor Solutions — $36.86bn (58% of revenue)**: custom AI accelerator chips and networking silicon (the Tomahave/Jericho switch families), plus long-tail chips for broadband, storage, wireless and industrial uses.
- **Infrastructure Software — $27.03bn (42% of revenue)**: largely VMware (acquired in FY2024), plus mainframe and cybersecurity software (CA, Symantec legacy businesses).

```

## The latest quarter is the story

The most recent reported quarter, **Q3 FY2026 (ended 2 Aug 2026, filed 10 Sep 2026)**, was extraordinary:

| Metric | Q3 FY26 | vs prior quarter | vs year ago |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | $29.59bn | +33.4% | **+85.5%** |
| Gross profit | $20.46bn | +32.7% | +91.1% |
| Operating income | $15.96bn | +47.9% | +171.0% |
| Net income | $13.09bn | +40.6% | +216.1% |

Margins in that quarter: gross margin 69.1% (keeps ~69¢ of every $1 of sales after making the product), operating margin 53.9% (keeps ~54¢ after running the whole business), net margin 44.2%. R&D spend was 9.8% of revenue — unusually low, because revenue grew far faster than R&D dollars.

The four most recent quarters show a steep acceleration: revenue went $18.0bn → $19.3bn → $22.2bn → $29.6bn. This is a sharp break from the last full fiscal year (FY2025 revenue $63.89bn, +23.9% YoY), so the current run-rate is well above the annual trend.

## Five-year annual picture

| Fiscal year end | Revenue | Net income | Operating margin | FCF margin |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2021-10-31 | $27.45bn | $6.74bn | 31.0% | 48.5% |
| 2022-10-30 | $33.20bn | $11.50bn | 42.8% | 49.1% |
| 2023-10-29 | $35.82bn | $14.08bn | 45.2% | 49.2% |
| 2024-11-03 | $51.57bn | $5.90bn | 26.1% | 37.6% |
| 2025-11-02 | $63.89bn | $23.13bn | 39.9% | 42.1% |

FY2024's low net income ($5.9bn despite higher revenue) reflects the VMware acquisition — purchase accounting and integration costs crushed reported profit that year; FY2025 shows the recovery. Free cash flow (operating cash flow minus capital spending — the cash the business actually generates after investing) was $26.9bn in FY2025, up 38.6% YoY, with capex under 1% of revenue. Broadcom is extraordinarily cash-efficient for a semiconductor company.

```

## Cash returns and balance sheet

In FY2025 Broadcom paid $11.14bn in dividends and $2.45bn in buybacks — $13.59bn total, comfortably covered by its $26.9bn free cash flow (a $13.3bn surplus). Shareholder equity jumped 20% to $81.3bn. Cash was $16.2bn. One gap: the verified data doesn't include a current total-debt figure for FY2025 (the balance-sheet tool found no compatible filed fact for short- or long-term debt that year), so I can't state present leverage — though the VMware deal was heavily debt-funded historically.

## How it compares

Against 187 Information Technology peers, Broadcom sits in the **85th percentile for 5-year revenue growth (21.7%/yr vs 9.4% median)** and the **94th percentile for net margin (36.2% vs 9.4% median)**. Its P/E of 43.8 is only ~11% above the sector median of 39.6 — modest for a company growing this fast. Peers like AMD (P/E 156) and Palantir (P/E 161) trade far richer.

## Valuation: what's priced in

At the 2 Oct 2026 close of **$355.14** (market cap ~$1.70tn, Yahoo Finance), a reverse DCF — which asks what growth rate today's price implies — says the market is pricing in roughly **23.4% annual free-cash-flow growth for the next decade**. For context, Broadcom's actual 5-year FCF growth has been 18.3%/yr. Scenario ranges: a bear case of ~10% growth implies ~62% downside; a bull case of ~26% growth implies ~23% upside. That's a descriptive range, not a price target.

**The read** — Broadcom's fundamentals right now are close to best-in-class: 86% YoY revenue growth, 54% operating margins, and a cash machine that funds dividends twice over. The tension is entirely in the price — at ~44x earnings the market has already booked several more years of AI-driven growth, so the investment case rests on whether the current quarter's explosive trajectory is structural rather than a cyclical peak.
